Online Hosted Link

If you've put a copy of this program online somewhere (a hosted link teachers can open in any browser, no file download needed), save it here — it'll show as a clickable link at the top of the guide below for anyone who opens this copy.

User Guide

Everything about setting up and using this program, from opening it for the first time to every tab and feature. Use the list below to jump to a section — this whole guide lives in the browser with your data, so it's always here, even offline.

1. Running the Program

This program is one self-contained file — everything it needs is built into it, and it works completely offline once it's open. Your data is stored inside whichever browser you open it in, on that specific device — it is not sent anywhere online (unless you choose the hosted-link option below, in which case the page itself is online, but your entered data still stays local to your browser).

On a Windows or Mac Computer

Double-click the downloaded .html file, or drag it into any browser window (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari all work). Bookmark the page once it's open so you can find it again quickly. If you move or rename the file, just open it the same way from its new location — nothing else changes.

On an iPad or iPhone

This is the trickiest part, because iOS restricts what a locally-saved HTML file is allowed to do — Safari generally won't run one directly from the Files app anymore. There are a few reliable workarounds, roughly easiest to most technical:

  • Documents by Readdle (easiest): install the free "Documents by Readdle" app from the App Store. Get the HTML file into its storage (download it there directly, or save it from the Files app's share sheet into Documents), then tap it — Documents has its own built-in browser that is allowed to run local HTML files fully, grades and all.
  • Host it online: since the restriction is specifically about local files, putting the file on any public web address sidesteps it entirely — it then opens in ordinary Safari like any website. Free options: Netlify Drop (app.netlify.com/drop — drag the file in, get an instant link) or GitHub Pages (needs a free GitHub account, but the link is permanent). Once hosted, save that link at the top of this page using the "Hosted Link" box above.
  • A Mac on the same WiFi: open Terminal on the Mac, navigate to the file's folder, and run python3 -m http.server 8000. On the iPad, open Safari and go to http://[Mac's IP address]:8000/filename.html — this is genuine Safari with zero restrictions, for as long as that Terminal window stays open.
  • Working Copy app: a git client with a built-in local web server — load the file in, hit Preview, and it serves the page straight into real Safari.

Whichever method you use, your grade data still lives inside that specific browser/app on that specific iPad — it doesn't automatically appear on other devices. Back up regularly (see the Backup section below), especially on iPad, since iOS can clear old, unused browser storage after about a week of inactivity.

Using an Online Hosted Link

If your school has put this program on a website (see the box at the top of this page), anyone with the link can open it in any browser on any device — no file to download or manage. This is often the simplest option for teachers who just want to click a link and start working. Data still stays local to whichever browser opens it; hosting the page online does not create a shared/synced database between different people's devices.

2. First-Time Setup

  1. Open the gear icon (top-right corner) to reach Settings. Enter your school's name and upload a logo — this appears in the app header and on every printed report card.
  2. Still in Settings, check the School Years list and make sure the current year is correct (add a new one if needed).
  3. Go to Subjects & Courses and review the default subjects — Math, Language Arts, Bible, and so on are already set up for grades 1–8, and a starter set of High School courses (Algebra I, Biology, etc.) is ready for grades 7–12. Edit, remove, or add subjects to match what you actually teach.
  4. Go to Students, click + Add Student, and add your roster — name, grade level, teacher, and whether they're Elementary or High School level.
  5. Start entering grades in Grade Entry, attendance in Attendance, and behavior ratings in Social Grading.

3. Dashboard

Your at-a-glance overview: every active student with their Q1–Q4 combined average, annual average, and total credits, in one table. Click any student's row to open a full-year detail popup — every subject, attendance, and social rating for the whole year on one screen. That popup has its own Print button, so you can hand someone a full-year summary without going through Report Cards.

4. Reports

Six independent report "slots," each with its own View, Chart Style, and filters — set them differently and each one remembers its own settings, so they stay exactly how you left them. Pick a View — One Student/All Subjects, One Student/One Subject by Quarter, One Subject/All Students, Grade-by-Grade Averages, Whole Class Trend, or (when Credits tracking is on) Credits Earned by Student or by School — then a Chart Style (bar, horizontal bar, line, or pie) and whatever filters apply (student, subject, quarter, grade level).

Columns: a dropdown above the reports lets you show them in 1, 2, 3, or 4 columns. Fewer columns means each report gets a wider, taller box — with just 1 column, every chart redraws noticeably larger and easier to read; the choice is remembered for next time.

Printing a report: each report card has its own Print This Report button for printing just that one. To print several at once, check Select to print on any reports you want, then use the Print Selected button at the top of the tab — each selected report prints on its own page, chart only (no dropdowns or controls).

5. Report Cards

Generates a printable report card booklet — designed to print on one landscape letter sheet, double-sided, then folded in half into a 4-page booklet:

PageWhat's on it
Front coverSchool logo, name, student info, grade, teacher, year, and a Bible verse/note (shared across all students, editable above the Generate button)
Inside-leftAcademic Grades (every quarter, always cumulative), Honor Roll badge, Attendance
Inside-rightBook Report — every completed book/assignment, organized by subject in two columns
Back coverSocial Development ratings (all 4 quarters), a note to parents, and a signature line — plus Book Report overflow if a student has more books than fit on the inside-right page alone

Every report is cumulative — printing Quarter 3 still shows Q1 and Q2 data alongside it, so the same booklet just fills in more each quarter. Use Print This Report for one student or Print All Active Students to run the whole class at once.

Which subjects show up: K-8 subjects (grades 1–8) always appear on the Academic Grades table, whether or not the student has any grades in them yet — every student in that grade takes the standard K-8 lineup. High School courses only appear if the student actually has grade entries for them this year, so a High School student's report doesn't get cluttered with every elective course configured for their grade level, only the ones they're actually taking.

Social Development page-fit: Social Development always prints on the inside-left page, right below Attendance. If a student has enough active courses and/or enough social categories have been added that it wouldn't normally fit, the whole page automatically shrinks — smaller text, tighter rows — so everything still lands on that one sheet instead of moving anywhere else. Nothing to configure.

Before printing: in your browser's print dialog, set orientation to Landscape, paper to Letter, turn on two-sided/duplex printing (flip on the short edge) if your printer supports it, and turn off "Headers and footers" — a browser setting outside this app's control, but switching it off removes the page URL/date/title the browser would otherwise print in the margins. Also look for a "Background graphics" checkbox and make sure it's on, or the colored shading and subject colors won't print.

The "Include school logo on the cover" checkbox lets you leave the logo off a particular run if needed — it's remembered for next time.

Credits column: if Credits tracking is turned off in Settings, the Credits column and "Credits Earned" row disappear from every report card automatically — nothing to configure per-printout.

6. High School Reporting & Planning

A dedicated tab for building out and tracking a High School student's course plan and credits toward graduation — sits alongside Report Cards, since it works with the same student data but is focused specifically on High School planning rather than quarterly grading.

Who shows up here: only active students in 8th grade or higher. A student appears in the Overview list automatically once they're marked High School level or have any High School course grade entries; they disappear the moment they're graduated, marked Inactive, or drop below 8th grade. To look up a graduated or inactive student's finished High School record, use the Full Report link from the Students tab instead (see below) — the High School tab itself is only ever a live, current-roster view.

Overview

A summary table of every eligible High School student, with their projected credits, earned credits, and progress percentage at a glance. Click any row (or its Open Plan button) to jump straight to that student's Plan & Progress tab, or click View Report to open their printable High School report directly.

Blank Planning Form: a Print Blank Planning Form button sits at the top of the High School tab, alongside the Overview and Plan & Progress sub-tab buttons — available from either sub-tab. It opens a preview popup first (not an immediate print), so you can see exactly what will print before it does; hit Print inside that popup when ready, or Close to back out. The form itself isn't tied to any one student's data — it's meant to be handed to a family to fill out by hand. It lists every course already set up under Subjects & Courses (High School folder), plus several blank lines for any course not yet on file, with columns for Credit Amount, Projected Year to Complete, and a Completed checkbox, plenty of room at the bottom for a signature, and blank lines for the student's name, anticipated graduation year, and a short written Purpose of My High School Education statement in the student's own words. The whole thing is sized to always print on a single page — the number of blank lines automatically shrinks (down to a minimum of 6) as more High School courses are set up, so it never runs onto a second page.

Plan & Progress

Pick a student, then:

  • High School Plan — add courses from the High School Courses list, each with a Grade Level and a Credit value (defaults to that course's High School Credit Value, set in Subjects & Courses, but editable per plan item). Every course starts Projected. Once it's actually done, click Mark Finished to move it from projected to finished — this is what awards its credit toward the student's earned total; click Move to Projected to undo that if needed.
  • Total Projected Credits and Credits Earned So Far update live as you build the plan and finish courses.
  • Progress Toward Plan — a bar showing earned credits against the total projected.
  • Courses & Averages — every planned course with its computed average grade (or letter, for letter-graded courses) and status (Not Started / In Progress / Finished), pulled from actual grade entries across all of that student's years.
  • View / Print Report — opens the same printable pop-up report as the Overview tab's per-row button.

Since students are tracked as separate records per school year (the same way Promote All works elsewhere), a High School plan is tied to the student's name, not a single year's record — it carries forward automatically as they're promoted from 9th through 12th grade.

7. Search

One box searches students, subjects, and grade entries all at once — type a student's name, part of a book title, or a subject name, and matching results appear grouped by category as you type. There's also a separate date field to find everything completed on a specific day. Use the Scope dropdown to narrow results to just one category. Search checks every school year at once, not just whichever one is currently selected. Student results include a Grade Entry button that jumps straight to that student.

8. Grade Entry

Split into two folders, Elementary and High School, each with its own Detailed Entry and Quick Entry sub-tabs — so High School courses never mix into a K-8 student's regular subjects, or the other way around. Anyone in 9th grade or higher is automatically treated as a High School student everywhere; an 8th grader stays in Elementary for their regular subjects, and additionally appears in the High School folder for any course marked Active on the High School tab.

  • Quick Entry — the fast path, in both folders. Pick a student, and every subject they take appears at once, each with just a few fields: Book #, Score, Week, and (if Credits tracking is on) Credits. Type the final score directly (no quiz/test breakdown) and hit Enter or the + button — it saves instantly and the form clears for the next book.
  • Detailed Entry — the full picture, with the full quiz/test/Daily breakdown. In Elementary, Student, Grade Level, and Subject filters at the top all combine together (AND logic) — same as the Daily Grades tab — so pick any two, or all three, to narrow the view any way you like. Each numeric subject shows a Daily box (leftmost, if the Daily Grading system is on), however many quiz columns it's configured for (0–4, set in Subjects & Courses), and a Test column. Rows go amber until every required score is filled in — amber rows aren't counted in averages yet. A new blank row appears automatically once you save one.

Anything entered in either mode is the exact same underlying data — it shows up identically in Dashboard, Report Cards, and Reports no matter which entry method you used.

A literal 0 doesn't count against the average: in any Daily, quiz, or Test box, entering a 0 is treated the same as leaving that box blank — it's left out of the Final Avg entirely rather than dragging the average down toward zero. This is useful for boxes that genuinely don't apply to a particular book/item without needing a whole different weighting setup. The row still shows as "complete" once every box has something in it (including a 0); a 0 just doesn't get counted in the math.

9. Daily Grades

A separate log for day-to-day grades (classwork, homework, participation, and the like) — kept apart from the quiz/test book entries in Grade Entry until you're ready to fold them in. Turn this feature on or off entirely in Settings (see below); when it's off, this tab and the Daily box in Grade Entry both disappear.

  • Filters: Student, Grade Level, and Subject filters at the top all combine together (AND logic) — pick any two, or all three, to narrow the view any way you like, alongside the usual Quarter selector.
  • Logging a grade: each subject box has a date field (defaults to today, editable for backdating) and a score field — press Enter or the + button to log it. Every entry logged shows in a running list with its own remove button, and a live Daily Avg updates above.
  • Push Average to Grade Entry: once you're ready, this button drops the current running average into that subject's current row in Grade Entry — landing in its own Daily box (separate from Quiz/Test), which then blends into that row's Final Avg using the subject's Daily Grade Weight (set in Subjects & Courses).
  • Archived batches: pushing an average also archives every entry that fed it into a collapsed, labelable line shown above the active list (e.g. label it "Unit 3" or "Quarter 1"). Click it to expand and review or edit the individual dated entries — the active list then starts clean for the next stretch of daily grades.

10. Attendance

  • By Week — the whole class, all 9 weeks of a quarter, in one wide table. An amber "fill whole column" row at the top lets you type one value and apply it to every student in that week at once — handy when most of the class was simply present.
  • By Student — all four quarters for one student, laid out as a 2×2 grid (Q1/Q2 on top, Q3/Q4 below), each with its own Weeks 1–9 and a running total, plus Semester and Year totals underneath.

11. Social Grading

Three sub-tabs:

  • Student Edit — rate one student, one quarter, across every category with a click of Excellent / Satisfactory / Needs Improvement.
  • Bulk Edit — a grid of every student × every category for the selected quarter, plus a "Quick Apply" tool to set one rating for the whole class at once.
  • Category Edit — add, rename, or remove rating categories. Categories can be nested under a parent (e.g. "Table Manners" under "Respect for Authority") the same way Spelling nests under Language Arts.

12. Students

Two sub-tabs, Active Students and Graduated / Inactive Students. There's no separate "Create / Edit" sub-tab — instead:

  • Click + Add Student at the top of the tab to add a new student.
  • Double-click any row in any student table (Active, Inactive, or the Archive) — or use its Edit button — to open that student in the same popup, pre-filled for editing: name, grade, teacher, Active/Inactive status, and Level (Elementary, High School, or Graduated).
  • Hit Save Student and the popup closes automatically. Clear resets the form without closing, and Close (or clicking outside the popup) dismisses it without saving.
  • Active Students — everyone currently active for the selected year, plus Promote All to Next Grade / New Year, which bumps every active student up a grade and copies them into a new school year you name.
  • Graduated / Inactive Students — students marked Inactive (still on record, just not currently attending) and, separately, an Archive of every Graduated student, from any year. Graduated students are hidden from every other tab in the app — Grade Entry, Attendance, Social Grading, Dashboard, Reports, Report Cards, High School — until you hit Restore on them here.

Full Report: in any student table, click a student's name (it's a link) to open a full multi-year report — one full-year report page for every school year they have a record for, plus a High School section at the end if they have any High School plan or course activity on record at all. It has its own Print button and works for any student regardless of current status, so it's the way to look up a graduated or inactive student's complete history.

13. Subjects & Courses

Two sub-tabs, K-8 and High School Courses, keep elementary subjects and high school courses in separate folders so they never mix together in one long list. There's no separate "Add / Edit" sub-tab anymore — instead:

  • Click + Add Subject at the top of the tab to add a new subject or course.
  • Double-click any row in either table (or use its Edit button) to open that subject in the same popup, pre-filled for editing.
  • Hit Save Subject and the popup closes automatically. Clear resets the form without closing, and Close (or clicking outside the popup) dismisses it without saving.

In that popup, you control:

  • Grading Type — Numeric (0–100) or Letter Grade (like Music, Art, Typing)
  • Sub-grade of another subject? — nest one subject under another, the way Spelling nests under Language Arts
  • Folder — K-8 or High School
  • Number of Quizzes (0–4), Quiz Weights, and Test Weight — each quiz and the test are averaged in proportion to their weight; the classic (Q1+Q2+Test×2)/4 formula is just 2 quizzes at weight 1 and a test at weight 2
  • Daily Grade Weight (shown when the Daily Grading system is on) — how much a Daily average pushed in from the Daily Grades tab counts toward a book row's Final Avg, relative to the quiz/test weights — e.g. a weight of 1 counts the same as one quiz
  • Default Credits (shown when Credits tracking is on) — pre-fills every new entry for that subject; set it to 0 to lock credits off entirely for a subject (Spelling defaults this way)
  • High School Credit Value (High School folder only) — the standard credit value this course is worth toward a diploma (e.g. 1.0 for a full-year course, 0.5 for a semester). This is separate from Default Credits above — Default Credits pre-fills per-book/assignment entries in regular grading, while High School Credit Value is what the High School tab uses when a course is added to a student's plan.
  • Category (High School folder only) — Math, Language Arts, Bible, Science, Social Studies, or Electives. Groups the High School Courses list and the course picker when planning a student's schedule, and can be used to sort the High School Courses table.
  • Applies to Grade Levels — which grades (1–12) see this subject at all

14. Settings

Reached through the gear icon in the top-right corner. Every section is a collapsible card that starts closed each time you open this tab — click a section's header to expand it. Sections appear in this order: School Information, School Years, Report Card Appearance, Merge In Another Teacher's File, Duplicate Entry Scanner, Export to Excel, Backup and Import, and Clear All Data. Backing up, restoring, exporting, and merging data each get their own full walkthrough in the next section since they're worth understanding well.

School Information is at the top and covers everything about how the school itself is set up, in three stacked groups within the one card:

  • School name, logo, and a Save Settings button — these appear in the app header and on every printed report card.
  • Daily Grading System — a checkbox (with its own Save button) that turns the whole Daily Grades feature on or off — run the program with just quiz/test grading, or with day-to-day grading added in, whichever fits your school. Turning it off hides the Daily Grades tab and the Daily box on Grade Entry rows; nothing is deleted, and everything reappears if you turn it back on.
  • Grading Periods, Honor Roll & Credits — one Save button covering: how many grading periods your school uses and how many weeks each one runs (defaults to 4 Quarters of 9 weeks); whether Honor Roll shows on report cards and the dashboard; and whether Credits are tracked at all. None of these take effect until you click Save, so you can adjust several at once and confirm together.

School Years: add a new year, or rename an existing one (fixes a typo without losing anything — every student, grade, attendance, and other record filed under it moves to the new name automatically) or delete one outright (permanently removes it and everything filed under it; always confirms first, and at least one year must remain).

Clear All Data (last section, outlined in red) also holds Delete Confirmations — a checkbox that controls whether you get an "Are you sure?" popup before routine deletes elsewhere in the app (grade entries, students, subjects, social categories, High School plan items, and duplicate cleanup). Turn it off if those popups feel slow when cleaning up a lot of records at once. This setting doesn't touch Clear All Data itself or deleting a school year, both of which always confirm no matter what, since they erase data permanently.

15. Backing Up, Restoring, Exporting, and Merging Data

Everything in this program lives in this specific browser's storage, on this specific device — nothing is sent anywhere online automatically. That makes backups genuinely important, not optional. All of this lives in Settings, under a few clearly separated cards.

What's Actually in a Backup File

A backup is a single .json file containing everything: every student across every school year, every subject and course you've configured, every grade entry, all attendance records, every social rating, your report-card cover notes, and your school name/logo. It's a complete snapshot — restoring one puts the program back to exactly the state it was in when that backup was made.

Backing Up (Backup Now)

  1. Open Settings (gear icon) → Backup and Import.
  2. Click Backup Now. Your browser downloads a file named something like school-data-backup-2026-11-01.json, dated automatically.
  3. Move that file somewhere safe — a cloud drive folder, a USB stick, wherever you keep important files. The Downloads folder alone isn't a real backup location; get a copy somewhere separate from this device.

How often: at minimum, after any significant chunk of grading work, and always before doing anything listed as risky below (Restore/Replace, Clear All Data, or merging in a file for the first time). Many teachers find it easiest to just make it a weekly habit.

Choose Default Backup Folder (Chrome or Edge on a computer only — this is a browser limitation, not something this program can change): lets you pick one folder once, and every future Backup Now saves straight into it automatically, no save dialog. On Safari, Firefox, or iPad, Backup Now will always use your browser's normal save prompt instead — which works fine, it's just one extra click each time.

Restoring a Backup (Restore / Replace)

This is destructive — read this before using it. Restore / Replace does not add a backup's data alongside what's already here; it completely wipes everything currently in this browser and replaces it with whatever is in the backup file you choose. Use it when you want to:

  • Move your data to a different computer or browser (back up on the old one, restore on the new one)
  • Undo a serious mistake by rolling back to an earlier dated backup
  • Start a fresh copy of the program from a known-good snapshot

If you just want to add another file's data without losing what's already here, you want Merge, not Restore — see below.

Merging In Another File (Adding Data Without Replacing Anything)

Unlike Restore, Merge adds a backup's students and grades into what you already have — nothing existing gets overwritten or deleted. This is the tool for combining multiple teachers' work into one master file, or bringing in a backup from another device without losing what's already on this one.

  1. Settings → Merge In Another Teacher's File → choose the .json backup file.
  2. Matching is done by first name + last name, within the same school year. If a student already exists in your file under that year, their grades from the merged file are added alongside whatever's already on record for them — the student itself isn't duplicated.
  3. If the same student's first+last name doesn't already exist in that year, they're added as a new student.
  4. High School plan items merge in too, keyed to the student's name the same way the rest of the High School tab is — a plan built in one teacher's file shows up correctly once merged in, and any student it touches appears on the High School tab immediately if they're currently active and 8th grade or higher.

Merging automatically checks for exact duplicates. As soon as a merge finishes, it checks everything the merge just added — grade entries and High School plan items alike — against what was already on file. If any of them are exact duplicates (same student, subject, quarter, book, and score for grade entries; same student, course, and grade level for a High School plan item), a review window pops up automatically listing each one with a Delete This One button, so you can clear out the extras right then instead of hunting for them later. If nothing looks duplicated, you just get a plain "Merge complete" message.

You can also run the standalone Duplicate Entry Scanner (right below the Merge card in Settings) any time — it checks your whole file for grade-entry duplicates, not just what a recent merge added, which is useful if you suspect a file was merged in more than once in the past.

Exporting to Excel — A Report, Not a Backup

Settings → Export to Excel produces a real, nicely formatted .xlsx workbook — six tabs covering Student Summary, Grades, Attendance, Social Grading, Subjects, and Students, with colored headers and sized columns, ready to open in Excel or Google Sheets.

Important distinction: this is for sharing, printing, or archiving a human-readable report — it is not something you can load back into the program later. Only a JSON backup file (from Backup Now) can be restored or merged back in. If you ever need to actually recover your data, it has to come from a .json backup, not an Excel export.

Clear All Data

Permanently erases every student, subject, grade, attendance record, and social rating in this browser, for every school year — not just the one currently selected. There is no undo. It requires typing DELETE exactly to confirm, on purpose, to make it hard to trigger by accident. Always back up first if there's any chance you'll want this data again. This section of Settings also holds the Delete Confirmations toggle (see above).

16. Running This With Multiple Teachers

Since this program has no server and no live sync, the practical way to combine several teachers' work into one master record is a periodic manual routine:

  1. Each teacher runs their own copy, on their own computer, entering grades for their own students.
  2. On a set schedule (e.g. monthly), every teacher clicks Backup Now and sends you the downloaded file.
  3. You open your own copy and use Merge In Another Teacher's File once per teacher file — this adds their students and grades into yours. Matching is done by first + last name within the same school year, so a student already in your file won't be duplicated.
  4. Run the Duplicate Entry Scanner afterward as a quick sanity check, especially if a file might have been merged more than once by accident.
  5. Click Backup Now yourself — that combined file is now your dated, master record.

17. Tips & Troubleshooting

  • Nothing is saving: your browser's storage may be full — this most often happens from a very large, uncompressed logo image. Logos are automatically resized now, but if you ever see a "storage is full" message, back up your data and consider clearing an old, no-longer-needed school year.
  • Colors don't print: look for a "Background graphics" checkbox in your browser's print dialog and turn it on.
  • iPad won't open the file: see the iPad section above — this is an iOS restriction, not a bug in the program.
  • A student disappeared from every tab: check Students → Graduated / Inactive — they may have been marked Graduated, which intentionally hides them everywhere except that tab until restored.
  • A student isn't showing up in the High School tab: that tab only lists active students in 8th grade or higher — check their grade level and Active/Inactive status on the Students tab. Graduated students are removed from it on purpose; use a student's Full Report link instead to see their finished High School record.
  • Always back up before a big change like Restore/Replace, Clear All Data, or merging in a file you haven't used before.

Add Subject
Numeric subjects are scored 0–100 from quiz/test entries. Letter subjects (like Music, Art, Typing) are graded directly by letter. Spelling-type subjects average separately from their parent subject and, by default, don't add their own credit.
How much a pushed Daily average counts toward the Final Avg.
HS Credit is separate from Default Credits, and is used on the High School tab.
Each quiz and the test are averaged in proportion to their weight — e.g. two quizzes at weight 1 and a test at weight 2 gives the test double influence, matching the classic (Q1+Q2+Test×2)/4 formula.
Pre-fills every new entry for this subject; set to 0 to disable.

School Information

▾

1. Basic Information

School Name Shown at the top of the sidebar, on report cards, and on every printed form.
Logo Image Optional — appears next to the school name and on report cards.

2. Grading Calendar

How the school year is divided up for grading. Most schools use the default — 4 Quarters of 9 weeks each (36 weeks total) — but any combination works.
4 periods = "Quarters" elsewhere in the app; any other count = "Periods."

3. Honor Roll

Show Honor Roll On report cards and the dashboard. Turn off if your school doesn't use one.
Manual overrides on a report card always take priority over these.

4. Credits Tracking

Track Credits On grade entries, report cards, and reports — separate from High School Credit Value, which always shows for diploma planning.
Turning this off hides the Credits field everywhere it normally appears. Nothing is deleted — existing credit values reappear right where they were if you turn it back on.
Sections 2–4 above are saved together — nothing takes effect until you click this button.

5. Daily Grading

Turn on the Daily Grading system Adds day-to-day grading alongside quiz/test grading. Turning this off hides the Daily Grades tab and column — nothing already saved is deleted.
Nothing here takes effect until you click Save.

School Years

▾
Rename moves all records with it. Delete removes a year permanently.

Report Card Appearance

▾
Controls the text sizes on the printed report card only — the one generated from the Report Cards tab (Academic Grades chart and section headings). This does NOT change the Dashboard's student-detail popup or the Full Multi-Year Student Report, which keep their own fixed sizing. The grade numbers/letters can be sized independently from the subject names so they stand out. Because the printed report card is a fixed-size sheet, very large sizes may cause it to compact more tightly (or not fit) for students with a lot of subjects — check the Report Cards tab after saving. Changes apply the next time you view or print a report card.
Sizes are in "rem" units — 1 = normal text size.

Merge In Another Teacher's File

▾
Each teacher runs their own copy of this file, on their own computer, fully offline, entering grades for their own students all year. At the end of the year (or whenever you want a combined view), have each teacher export their backup (below) and send you the file. Use "Merge In A File" below, once per teacher file, to combine them all into one master copy — this ADDS their students and grades into yours rather than replacing anything.

Matching is done by student first + last name within the same school year. A student already in your file won't be duplicated; their grades from the merged file will be added alongside anything already on record for them.
Only merge each teacher's file once — merging the same file twice will duplicate their grade entries.

Duplicate Entry Scanner

▾
Checks for grade entries that look like exact duplicates — same student, subject, quarter, book, and score — which is the most common thing to end up with after merging in a teacher's file more than once, or merging the same file twice by mistake. Nothing is deleted automatically; each duplicate found gets its own "Delete This One" button so you choose which copy to keep.

Export to Excel

▾
Creates a real, nicely formatted .xlsx workbook — a tab each for the Student Summary, Grades, Attendance, Social Grading, Subjects, and Students — with colored headers, sized columns, and subjects tinted to match their colors elsewhere in the app. This is a report to share or archive, not a backup — use "Backup Now" below to restore your data later.

Backup and Import

▾
This program stores everything in this specific browser, on this specific computer — it is NOT sent anywhere online, and it is NOT automatically backed up unless you set that up below.

Best practice: back up at the end of every day you enter grades, and definitely at the end of every quarter. Keep the file somewhere outside the browser itself — a shared drive, USB stick, or email it to yourself.
Back Up Now Saves everything to a file you keep somewhere safe.
Restore / Replace All Data Wipes what's currently here and replaces it entirely with a backup file — for moving to a new computer or undoing a mistake.

Automatic Backups — Chrome or Edge on a computer only

Default Backup Folder Checking…
Live Backup Live Backup is off.
Once a folder is chosen, "Backup Now" saves straight there instead of asking each time. Turning on Live Backup also quietly saves a file called school-data-live-backup.json into that folder a couple of seconds after every change — no clicking needed. In Safari, Firefox, or on iPad, backups will keep using the normal save prompt instead.

Troubleshooting

Refresh App Reloads the screen in place — everything already saved is kept. Use if something looks stuck.

Clear All Data

▾
Skips the "Are you sure?" prompt on routine deletes. "Clear All Data" always still confirms.
This permanently erases every student, subject, grade, attendance record, and social rating in this browser — for all school years, not just the current one. There is no undo. Export a backup first if there's any chance you'll want this data again.
